messages:
sophia: Heads-up — RFC followup: proposing a lightweight 'safeguard-arbitrator' service to centralize canary/A-B decisions and automatic fallback. want to capture interface boundaries and long-term refactor path here.
jamal: interested. quick Q — what surface area are we talking about? is this replacing router heuristics or augmenting them?
sophia: augmenting. idea is: orchestrator (canary controller) expresses intent -> arbitrator evaluates signals + policy -> arbitrator issues leases/decisions -> router enforces routing. router keeps a local cache of leases. NOT a full rewrite of router logic, just a clear RPC/stream contract. example response shape we want:

```yaml
decision: allow
fallback_variant: v1
reason: warmup_done
ttl_seconds: 300
graceful_drain: true
```

mike: main tradeoff is extra RPC hop for new sessions which could bump p95. can we avoid per-request RPCs? cache aggressively?
sophia: yes, cache at router keyed by route+session-id. caches respect ttl and can be invalidated via a watch stream. for long-lived sessions we pin the lease until session end or explicit release.

ray: how do we signal mid-canary aborts (perf or quality regressions)? need an atomic switch to fallback without traffic oscillation.
sophia: telemetry contract: arbitrator consumes traces/metrics and can emit an abort with reason codes (latency_spike, error_rate, quality_regression). it publishes aborts on the watch stream + we expose a pubsub websocket for low-latency routers. router must implement atomic swap: apply fallback_variant, set graceful_drain, and prevent new sessions to canary for N seconds.

jamal: what about private/offline installs where arbitrator might be unreachable? don't want global outages.
sophia: fallback-first behavior: router has a local policy engine with conservative defaults. if arbitrator unreachable, router uses local rules, e.g., cap canary to 0.5% and fail-closed or fail-open controlled by customer config. we should add a 'local-fallback-mode' flag per deployment.

mike: can we see a compact DSL example for policies? makes reviews easier.
sophia: sure, POC DSL snippet:

```yaml
policy_name: perf-safe-canary
match:
  service: "text-gen"
  model_family: "redwood-*-llama"
signals:
  - latency.p95 < 120
  - error_rate < 0.005
actions:
  - ramp_to: 10% over 30m
  - abort_if: latency.p95 increases by > 30%
exposure:
  initial: 2%
  max: 20%
```
deploy-bot: canary/alpha rolled to 2% traffic for variant v2-service (id:canary-2026-03-20) — started 3891234568 :rocket:

ray: ops note — make sure our probe/oracles run warmup and send separate warmup metrics. cold-start noise killed one canary last quarter.
jamal: long-term thought: unify arbitrator signals with autoscaler decisions so canary judge and scaler don't fight each other. expose composite metrics upstream.
sophia: agreed. I'll draft an RFC with the API surface: POST /lease/query, GET /lease/watch (stream), POST /lease/release, and a metrics schema (latency/error/quality). target: RFC by EOW for architecture + runtime review. adding perf budget for arbitration RPCs as a requirement.

mike: +1 on RFC. also add a perf SLA: arbitration RPC p95 < 10ms within region, and a fallback path if exceeded. :eyes:

sophia: noted. next steps: I'll sketch the API proto and a minimal reference impl inside eng-runtime, then sync with eng-platform on rollout UI + console hooks. thanks everyone for quick feedback!
